questions.problem: A glacier moves $49$ feet in $14$ months, moving at a constant rate. What is the speed of the glacier?
questions.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in feet per month, we divide the number of feet $49,$ by the number of months, $14.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{49}{14} & =\frac{49÷7}{14÷7} \\  & =\frac{7}{2} \\  & =7÷2 \\  & =3.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the glacier is $3.5$ feet per month.

questions.problem: A spacecraft traveled for $15$ seconds at a constant speed of $12$ kilometers per second. Find the distance covered by the spacecraft.
questions.worked_solution:
The speed is $12$ kilometers per second. To find the distance covered in $15$ seconds, we multiply the speed by $15.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{distance} & =\text{speed}\cdot \text{time} \\  & =12\times 15 \\  & =180.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the spacecraft covered $180$ kilometers in $15$ seconds.

questions.problem: A jet ski traveled $3\,960$ meters at a constant speed of $660$ meters per minute. For how long was the jet ski in motion?
questions.worked_solution:
The speed is $660$ meters per minute. To find the time it took the jet ski to cover $3\,960$ meters, we divide the distance by $660.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{3\,960}{660} \\  & =\frac{3\,960÷60}{660÷60} \\  & =\frac{66}{11} \\  & =66÷11 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the jet ski was in motion for $6$ minutes.

questions.problem: It takes $20$ minutes for a slug to crawl $90$ centimeters at a constant pace. How much time does it take for the slug to crawl $450$ centimeters?
questions.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in centimeters per minute, we divide the number of centimeters, which is $90,$ by the number of minutes, $20.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{90}{20} & =\frac{90÷10}{20÷10} \\  & =\frac{9}{2} \\  & =9÷2 \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the slug is $4.5$ centimeters per minute. 

To find the time it took the slug to cover $450$ centimeters, we divide the distance by $4.5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{450}{4.5} \\  & =\frac{450\cdot 10}{4.5\cdot 10} \\  & =\frac{4\,500}{45} \\  & =\frac{45\cdot 100}{45} \\  & =100.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the slug $100$ minutes to crawl $450$ centimeters.

canonical_examples.problem: It takes $5$ days for the Earth to travel $13$ million kilometers around the Sun. How much time does it take for the Earth to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in millions of kilometers per day, we divide the number of million kilometers, $13,$ by the number of days, $5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{5} & =13÷5 \\  & =2.6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the Earth is $2.6$ million kilometers per day. 

To find the time it takes the Earth to cover $52$ million kilometers, we divide the distance by $2.6.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{52}{2.6} \\  & =\frac{52\times 10}{2.6\times 10} \\  & =\frac{520}{26} \\  & =520÷26 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the Earth $20$ days to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
**Speed** is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*.

We can calculate the speed of a moving object using the following equation:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

For example, suppose that a car travels $80$ miles in $2$ hours at a constant rate. What is the speed of the car? 

To find the speed (in miles per hour), we divide the number of miles, $80,$ by the number of hours, $2.$ This gives

$$
\dfrac{80}{2} = 40.
$$

Therefore, the speed of the car is $40$ miles per hour.

tutorials.name: Calculating the Distance Traveled by an Object
tutorials.problem:
Let's return to the example of a car traveling at ${\color{red}{40}}$ miles per hour. 

If the car travels at this speed, it covers  a distance of ${\color{red}{40}}$ miles *every hour*. Therefore, we can deduce the following:

- after ${\color{blue}{1}}$ hour, the car covers a distance of ${\color{red}{40}}\times{\color{blue}{1}} = 40$ miles

- after ${\color{blue}{2}}$ hours, the car covers a distance of ${\color{red}{40}}\times{\color{blue}{2}} = 80$ miles

- after ${\color{blue}{3}}$ hours, the car covers a distance of ${\color{red}{40}}\times{\color{blue}{3}} = 120$ miles

- after ${\color{blue}{4}}$ hours, the car covers a distance of ${\color{red}{40}}\times{\color{blue}{4}} = 160$ miles

- $\cdots$

This suggests the following formula:

$$
\text{distance} = \text{speed} \times \text{time}
$$

We can use this formula to calculate the distance traveled by an object moving at a constant speed.

For instance, suppose an elevator traveled for $1.5$ minutes at a constant speed of $120$ feet per minute. What distance is covered by the elevator?

The speed is $120$ feet per minute. To find the distance covered in $1.5$ minutes, we multiply the speed by $1.5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{distance} & =\text{speed}\times \text{time} \\  & =120\times 1.5 \\  & =180.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elevator covered a distance of $180$ feet.

tutorials.name: Calculating the Total Time an Object is in Motion
tutorials.problem:
Let's recall the formula relating distance to speed and time:

$$
\text{speed} \times \text{time} = \text{distance}
$$

Using the relationship between multiplication and division, we can write this equation as

$$
\text{time} = \text{distance} \div \text{speed}
$$

which is equivalent to the formula

$$
\text{time} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}.
$$

We can use this formula to calculate the time taken for an object moving at a particular speed to cover a certain distance. 

For example, suppose a plane flew for $3\,120$ kilometers at a constant speed of $520$ kilometers per hour. For how long was the plane in motion?

To determine the time the plane was in motion, we divide the distance, $3\,120$ kilometers, by the speed, $520$ kilometers per hour. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{3\,120}{520} \\  & =\frac{3\,120÷10}{520÷10} \\  & =\frac{312}{52} \\  & =312÷52 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the plane was in motion for $6$ hours.
